title: Cokret Standard Event Payloads
description: Definitions bundle for common payload contracts used by registered ck.* Event.kind values. The root schema is intentionally generic and MUST NOT be used as a complete payload validator. Event validators MUST validate the full Event Envelope and dispatch by Event.kind to the matching $defs payload class using artifacts/registry/event-kind-registry.json.

member_delivery_binding.description: Per-Realm binding of a member to a concrete delivery target service. Authoritative source for Realm-scoped event / sync / to-device / push / key-package delivery; sender MUST NOT consult the actor's DID Document service entry as an alternative resolution path when this binding is present. Pairwise / unlinkability use-cases are orthogonal — see identity-did.md and pairwise DID guidance.

recipient_service_did.description: service DID of the recipient Principal Server for this member in this Realm.

recipient_service_type.description: v1 only allows principal_server. Notary / shared Sync Service are addressed by Realm-level sync_endpoints, not by member-level delivery_binding.

binding_scope.description: v1 only allows realm-scoped bindings. Organization-wide or DID-global bindings are out of v1 scope; they would be expressed by Realm policy + organization registry instead.

binding_source.description: How the binding was determined at join time. 'explicit' = user / admin chose; 'did_document_default' = resolved from invitee DID Document (only allowed when Realm policy enables fallback); other values are policy-driven.

delivery_modes.description: Explicit allow-list of delivery modes for this binding. Empty / absent is NOT permitted; implementations declaring a 'full' member SHOULD list all five values.

service_endpoint.description: Optional cached HTTPS endpoint of recipient_service_did at resolved_at. Diagnostic / fast-path hint only; sender MUST re-resolve via DID Document before federation transactions and SHOULD verify endpoint matches the service DID's current binding.

did_document_digest.description: Canonical hash of invitee's DID Document at resolved_at. Required when binding_source = did_document_default.

resolved_at.description: Wall-clock time at which the binding was resolved. Always required so that downstream verifiers can decide whether the resolved state is still acceptable under their freshness policy.

service_acceptance_ref.description: Reference to the recipient service's prior service_acceptance / endorsement Event. Required when binding_source = explicit or organization_policy; reducer MUST verify the referenced Event is signed by recipient_service_did and its scope covers this Realm.

holder_proof_ref.description: Reference to the member's DID proof (challenge-response) that bound the DID to recipient_service_did at the auth/account layer. Required when the member did not submit the join Control Move directly from a session at recipient_service_did.

policy_event_ref.description: Reference to the Realm / Join / Organization policy revision that authorised this binding. Required when binding_source ∈ {join_policy, organization_policy, realm_policy}.

expires_at.description: Optional expiry. After this timestamp the binding is no longer usable for delivery; senders MUST quarantine pending events and the member MUST submit a rebind Move (same-state join self-transition) carrying a fresh binding. Sender behaviour is fail-closed: MUST NOT fall through to DID Document on expiry.

seal_frontier.description: Accepted Seal coverage expressed as event_digest hash values, not ck:event typed ids. The hash algorithm is the enclosing Realm or control stream hash profile.

board_space_id.description: A Space with kind=board. Pattern matches any ck:space:; kind invariant enforced by reducer/profile.

track_name.description: Flow track key for Message payloads. Mirrors message.schema.json#/properties/track_name: v1 Message payloads are restricted to 'discussion'.

not.$comment: Reject discriminator field name `type`, composite child array name `blocks`, and byte-count field `size`. The discriminator is `kind`, the composite child array is `parts`, and byte counts use `size_bytes` (see schemas/message.schema.json and forbidden-wire-fields.json `blocks/content_block_composite`).

message_metadata.description: Extensible user-readable Message metadata. In MLS / E2EE realms this object is encrypted as encrypted_metadata unless the Realm explicitly opts into plaintext metadata.

not.$comment: Reducer-owned fields stay top-level and MUST NOT be mirrored inside metadata.

verification_method.description: DID URL of a concrete verification method. Bare DIDs are not valid where a key binding is required.

agent_key_id.description: Stable key identifier within the agent DID. Prefer the DID URL verification method id when available.

device_cross_signing_binding.description: SSK signature binding a ck.device.authorize payload's device_public_key to the principal's accepted cross-signing generation. Canonical signing input is defined in zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §5.2.

verification_method.description: DID URL of the self-signing key that signed the device trust binding.

device_bootstrap_binding.description: Bootstrap-only binding for the first ck.device.authorize event signed by the DID inception key before any ck.cross_signing.publish exists. Receivers MUST accept this only under the inception bootstrap rules in zh/identity/key-management.md §5.0.1 and zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §5.3.

patch_path.description: Cokret field patch path. Segments are snake_case identifiers, optional stable-key selectors (such as profile-declared named-collection arrays of the form `<field>[<key>=<value>]`), or backtick-quoted literals; numeric array indexes are not part of ck.patch.v1. v1 standard schemas no longer use stable-key selectors — Flow tracks is now a map keyed by track name, so paths like `tracks.discussion.profile` are plain object segments.

patch_value.description: A plain value is shorthand for {"$op":"set","value":...}. Objects containing $op MUST be patch_operation objects.

not.$comment: Object kind is derived from the typed-id prefix on `id`; `type` is a banned field name.

object_snapshot.description: Embedded object snapshot inside an Event payload. Object kind is derived from the typed-id prefix on `id`; there is no separate `type` field.

generic_standard_payload.description: Generic fallback shape used only inside Event Envelope kind dispatch and tooling diagnostics. It rejects the `type` field but does not close kind-specific fields; validators MUST NOT accept a standard Event solely because its payload validates against this definition.

not.$comment: Standard ck.* event payloads use kind (envelope) + payload schema discriminators. `type` is a banned field name here to keep schema validation aligned with reducer behavior.

notary_fault_equivocation_payload.description: Notary equivocation evidence: two Seals signed by signer_id that violate the slot rule (same (realm_id, notary_seq) with different canonical bytes, or notary_seq=k+1 not descending from the same signer's notary_seq=k). Admission is verification-only: the two conflicting notary signatures are the complete authorization; no capability grant is consulted. See authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 7.1.

notary_fault_censorship_payload.description: Notary censorship evidence: a signed control-plane receipt whose event digest is provably absent from the obliged Seal's control_event_set_root and that received neither signed-reject nor defer. Does NOT automatically disqualify the notary; adds an audit fault record. See authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 7.2.

receipt.description: The signed control-plane receipt issued under receipt_sla_ms (event_digest, received_at, receipt_seq, issuer, signature).

seal_ref.description: The Seal that was obliged to include / signed-reject / defer the receipted Control Move.

non_membership_proof.description: Sorted-neighbor non-membership proof for the receipted event digest against seal_ref's control_event_set_root.

missing_rejection_or_defer_proof.description: Optional structured evidence that no signed-reject / defer covering the receipt exists in the obliged window.

realm_create_payload.description: Create payload uses the full Realm object schema for wire validation. Semantic validation MUST require payload.object.created_by to match the top-level actor_id and payload.object.created_at to match the top-level created_at before acceptance.

space_create_payload.description: Create payload uses the full Space object schema for wire validation. Semantic validation MUST require payload.object.created_by to match the top-level actor_id and payload.object.created_at to match the top-level created_at before acceptance.

flow_create_payload.description: Create payload uses the full Flow object schema for wire validation. Semantic validation MUST require payload.object.created_by to match the top-level actor_id and payload.object.created_at to match the top-level created_at before acceptance.

circle_create_payload.description: Create payload uses the Circle object schema for wire validation. Reducer validation MUST require payload.object.created_by to match top-level actor_id and payload.object.created_at to match top-level created_at, then enforce parent Realm encryption floor. When payload.object.encryption_profile='mls_rfc9420', the reducer derives the independent MLS group binding for (realm_id, circle_id). payload.object.mls_group_ref is reducer-derived and MUST NOT be actor supplied.

morph_create_payload.description: Create payload uses the full Morph object schema for wire validation. Semantic validation MUST require payload.object.created_by to match the top-level actor_id and payload.object.created_at to match the top-level created_at before acceptance.

object_stage_set_payload.description: Shared base shape for ck.<kind>.stage.set events. Each concrete stage_set payload class (flow_stage_set_payload / morph_stage_set_payload) extends this base by pinning the object-id field (flow_id / morph_id) and is referenced from event-envelope.schema.json conditional routing. The stage enum is the protocol-level 8-value set defined in zh/models/common-fields.md §5.3.2; profile MUST NOT extend or override the enum. Reducer hard invariants are listed in zh/models/common-fields.md §5.3.3 (terminal state freeze, non-active reject, reducer-derived stage_changed_at, same-value no-op, single-source via this event). The payload intentionally does NOT carry a reason / note / explanation field: this event log is the audit source (actor_id + created_at), and human-readable explanation belongs in a Message on an associated discussion track that 'references' this event. expected_stage compiles to a cell head_eq precondition and provides optimistic concurrency; omission is equivalent to no CAS.

expected_stage.description: Optional CAS precondition: when present, reducer compiles it to a cell head_eq comparison against the cell's current value. Mismatch yields failed_precondition reason=stage_cas_mismatch. Same semantics as ck.flow.watch.set's expected_value.

not.$comment: Reason / note / explanation fields are intentionally rejected. Stage transitions audit through the event log; human-readable rationale belongs in a Message on the discussion track that references this event.

flow_stage_set_payload.description: Payload class for ck.flow.stage.set. Mutates Flow.stage / Flow.stage_changed_at. Intentionally carries no reason field — see object_stage_set_payload description and zh/models/flow-and-message.md §3.2.

not.$comment: Mirror of object_stage_set_payload guard. Reason-style fields are forbidden; rationale belongs in a discussion-track Message.

morph_stage_set_payload.description: Payload class for ck.morph.stage.set. Mutates Morph.stage / Morph.stage_changed_at. Intentionally carries no reason field — see object_stage_set_payload description and zh/models/morph.md §2.

morph_schema_migrate_payload.description: Migration of a Morph's schema_refs[] under the schema-evolution policy (zh/models/morph.md §4.1 S3). Distinct from ck.morph.update — schema_refs[] changes MUST go through this event so the migration is auditable, capability-gated, and carries an explicit compatibility class. Reducer MUST verify the actor holds the ck.morph.schema_migrate capability (or the Realm-declared equivalent) at the event's frontier; missing capability yields capability_denied. Reducer MUST reject compatibility_class ∈ {breaking, transformation} unless the Realm declares ck.profile.morph.schema_migration_transformations.v1 (yielding morph_schema_refs_transformation_unsupported otherwise). Reducer MUST verify from_schema_refs[] matches the Morph's current schema_refs[] at apply time (yielding failed_precondition otherwise). The event's own requirements.schema[] MUST include the union of from_schema_refs[] and to_schema_refs[] so readers can resolve both versions during overlap. Each transformation_rules[] entry SHOULD describe a deterministic, replay-safe per-field mapping (rename, type widening, default backfill, etc.); the rule object shape is governed by the Realm-declared ck.profile.morph.schema_migration_transformations.v1 profile.

from_schema_refs.description: Expected current schema_refs[] of the Morph at apply time. Reducer MUST set-equal-compare against the Morph's state and reject mismatches as failed_precondition (semantic: optimistic concurrency on schema_refs).

to_schema_refs.description: Desired schema_refs[] after migration. MUST be a registered set of schema profile ids resolvable at apply time.

compatibility_class.description: additive: to_schema_refs[] only adds optional fields / lookup-compatible profile refs; no historical event needs reinterpretation. breaking: to_schema_refs[] removes or tightens fields; future events follow new schema but historical events keep validating under from_schema_refs[]. transformation: a per-event data transform is needed to map old payload shape to new (requires explicit transformation rules). Core reducers MUST accept additive only; breaking and transformation require the ck.profile.morph.schema_migration_transformations.v1 opt-in Realm profile.

transformation_rules.description: Required when compatibility_class='transformation'. Each entry MUST describe a deterministic, replay-safe per-field mapping (rename, type widening, default backfill, etc.). The rule object shape is governed by ck.profile.morph.schema_migration_transformations.v1 (see profile description in conformance-profiles.json).

migration_evidence.description: Optional seal / witness evidence justifying the migration (e.g., governance proposal id, audit trail seal). The event's authorization_ref carries the formal capability gate; migration_evidence is for human reviewers.

actor_profile_create_payload.description: Initial actor profile payload. In CBA/Lattice state, the profile cell subject is payload.object.id.

account_data_set_payload.description: Payload for ck.account_data.set. Writes one holder-private account-data key; the value may be plaintext inside an already private envelope, encrypted account-data material, or a tombstone.

account_blocklist_payload.description: Payload for ck.account.blocklist. Holder-private personal blocklist state; it never enters shared Realm state or federation payloads.

object_patch_payload.description: Generic patch payload for object families that do not define a narrower id-specific payload. The target object is single-sourced by target_ref; object_ref and target-less patch forms from earlier drafts are not canonical.

profile_realm_override_payload.description: Realm-scoped actor profile override payload for ck.profile.realm_override. target_ref is the Actor Profile being overridden; target_realm_id is the Realm where the override applies.

circle_patch_payload.description: Payload class for ck.circle.update. Patch path MUST NOT contain realm_id, encryption_profile, mls_group_ref, state, state_changed_at, created_by, or created_at; reducer enforces the path-level lock and semantic policy floor checks.

space_patch_payload.description: Payload class for ck.space.update. Patches Space metadata (title, rank, kind-specific fields) on the Space identified by space_id. Per operations-sync.md §7.3 / §9.3 and realm-and-space.md §3.3, ck.space.update only mutates the Space's own metadata; it MUST NOT PATCH top-level state (archive/restore go through ck.space.archive / ck.space.restore) and MUST NOT move Flows (ck.flow.move / ck.flow.reorder). Reducer rejects update on a non-active Space (reason=space_not_active) — see conformance-vectors.md §6.7.

object_lifecycle_payload.description: Generic lifecycle payload for Flow / Circle / Morph archive-restore-tombstone style events. The target object is single-sourced by target_ref; target_state may describe the intended lifecycle result but cannot replace the target object reference.

circle_member_state_payload.description: Payload for ck.circle.member.state. Uses the same membership_state enum as ck.member.state (Realm), scoped to a Circle; reducer MUST verify actor_id is a `join` member of the parent Realm before any transition to `join`, MUST gate `knock` on Circle join_rule=request, and MUST reject self-unban/self-unremove paths.

circle_seal_commit_payload.description: Reducer-derived payload for ck.circle.seal_commit. Commits an opaque Circle sub-seal head digest into the parent Realm Seal stream at the profile-defined cadence.

restricted_policy_digest.description: Required when value=restricted. Digest of the effective ck.realm.history_sharing_policy value that defines restricted history visibility.

default_key_share.description: Baseline key-share rule before restricted_rules are evaluated. event_time_visibility still requires T0 history visibility, current safety policy, and receiver device checks.

reason_code.description: Machine-readable account status diagnostic. Values that cross service or federation boundaries MUST be registered in error-code-registry.json reason_codes (for example deactivation_federation_incomplete).

supersedes_status_event_id.description: Event id of the ck.account.status event being superseded. Required by zh/identity/account-lifecycle.md §3 rule 2 when lowering severity (e.g. back to active after appeal). MUST NOT be used to downgrade erasure_pending (reason_code erasure_pending_is_terminal).

space_state_transition_payload.description: Payload for ck.space.archive and ck.space.restore. The target Space is expressed on payload.space_id; top-level target_ref is a rejected field on Event envelopes.

space_object_tombstone_payload.description: Payload for ck.space.tombstone. Realm tombstone uses its separate Realm lifecycle payload; Space tombstone targets payload.space_id.

membership_state.description: Canonical membership state enum shared by ck.member.state (Realm) and ck.circle.member.state (Circle). Single source of truth: Realm and Circle membership use the identical value set; they MUST NOT diverge. `knock` denotes a pending join request (Realm Join Policy / Circle join_rule=request); see governance/join-policy.md §9 and models/circle.md §9.1.

gate_proofs.description: Join-policy gate proofs evaluated by governance/join-policy.md before accepting membership=join. maxItems aligns with the gates 1..16 bound in join_policy_payload; see zh/conformance/scalability-constraints.md.

member_identity_update_payload.description: Payload for ck.member.identity.update. Append-only replacement event for one Realm-scoped member display/subject projection segment. Service-visible metadata names the segment and the prior events it replaces; the segment body is plaintext or the original encrypted envelope and MUST contain the complete data for that segment. Handle lifecycle is excluded from this event and is governed by ck.schema.handle_claim.v1 issuer claims.

segment.description: v1 core defines a single full MemberIdentity segment. Narrower segments require a future schema/profile revision that extends this enum or defines a new payload schema; v1 receivers MUST reject unknown segment values.

replaces.description: Prior ck.member.identity.update events in the same (realm_id, actor_id, segment) that this event supersedes for current profile projection. Referenced events remain immutable history.

payload_digest.description: sha256 over RFC 8785 JCS canonical JSON of the replaced event's full payload.identity_payload carrier wrapper ({member_identity: ...} or {encrypted_payload: ...}). Prevents replacing a different payload under a reused or confused event id.

identity_payload_digest.description: sha256 over RFC 8785 JCS canonical JSON of the exact identity_payload carrier object. It is a cache invalidation key, not a substitute for signature or MLS verification.

expected_state_digest.description: Optional optimistic concurrency guard for the current effective set of this (realm_id, actor_id, segment). When present, it MUST equal the writer-observed effective-set digest before applying this event: sha256 over RFC 8785 JCS canonical JSON {realm_id, actor_id, segment, effective_events:[{event_id, segment, payload_digest}]}, with effective_events sorted by (segment,event_id). It is not the identity_payload_digest and not a roster member_display_state_digest.

data_classes.description: Closed machine-checkable classes of plaintext or reversible derived content this service may receive. Human-readable purposes do not replace this field.

join_policy_payload.$comment: Value-shape schema for the realm.join_policy.v1 cell (written as a sub-component of ck.realm.policy_components). Structural validation is JSON Schema; property-level gate_id uniqueness within gates[] cannot be expressed in pure JSON Schema 2020-12, so it is enforced by (a) reducer rejection with reason_code=join_policy_duplicate_gate_id and (b) tools/lint_artifacts.py check_join_policy_gate_id_uniqueness over fixtures and Markdown examples. uniqueItems below catches whole-object duplicates as a baseline. See zh/governance/join-policy.md §3 / §3.1.

application_ttl.description: Join application pending lifetime as an ISO 8601 duration, e.g. PT168H.

cooldown_after_reject.description: Minimum interval before the same actor may reapply after rejection, as an ISO 8601 duration, e.g. PT72H.

read_receipt_policy_payload.$comment: Payload for ck.realm.read_receipt_policy. Closed object (additionalProperties=false) so that typos in the privacy-floor escape switch `allow_child_privacy_tightening_against_required` cause schema_violation rather than silent acceptance. The enclosing Event envelope already carries `realm_id`; the payload does NOT duplicate it. `minProperties: 1` aligns with the generic state_payload branch in event-envelope.schema.json (ck.realm.* policy events): an empty `{}` payload is semantically identical to never writing the event (cell stays null with the same effective defaults), so it MUST be schema_violation rather than a silent no-op. See zh/discovery/read-receipts.md §2.5.

allow_child_privacy_tightening_against_r.description: Privacy-floor escape switch. Defaults to false. When the parent policy sets disclosure='required' and this field is true, a child Realm MAY tighten disclosure to 'optional' or 'disabled'. Misspellings (e.g., a missing underscore) cause schema_violation because additionalProperties=false; runtime mismatches yield read_receipt_compliance_floor_violated.

allow_public_receipts_on_world_readable.description: Opt-in switch for the visibility='public' + history_visibility='world_readable' combination. Defaults to false. When false the reducer MUST reject that combination; when true the reducer admits it with a warning. See zh/discovery/read-receipts.md §2.5.1.

message_create_payload.description: Payload for ck.message.create. If content/encrypted_content contains an audience_mention AST node (for example @all or @here), reducer admission and notification dispatch MUST additionally enforce ck.message.mention.broadcast plus the audience policy / max_recipient / rate-limit rules in zh/models/flow-and-message.md §9.4.3. @here maps to audience="flow_engaged" and is not presence-filtered.

allOf.$comment: ck.message.create payload MUST NOT carry revision_root. Reducer initializes revision_root := id on create; only ck.message.revise events may set it. See zh/models/flow-and-message.md §9 and forbidden-wire-fields.json `revision_root/message_create_payload`.

expiry.description: Optional disappearing-message expiry contract for ck.profile.disappearing.v1. Expiry is projection / retention semantics and MUST NOT be treated as redaction.

message_revise_payload.description: Payload for ck.message.revise. Revisions that introduce new direct mentions MAY generate mention notifications only when the implementation can compare against the previous accepted visible revision. Revisions that introduce an audience_mention AST node (including @all / @here mappings) MUST satisfy the same ck.message.mention.broadcast and policy gates as create.

track_name.description: Active track_name of the target Flow. Optional on revise/redact: when omitted, reducers MUST resolve from the existing message identified by message_id / target_ref / revision_of. When present, MUST equal that resolved track_name.
Active track_name of the redacted message's parent Flow. Optional: when omitted, reducers MUST resolve from the existing message. When present, MUST equal that resolved track_name.

event_ref.description: Calendar event Flow id; encoded as a ck:flow: typed id.

reaction_payload.description: Reducer input for ck.reaction.add and ck.reaction.remove. OR-Set membership is keyed on (actor_id, target_ref, key); a remove tombstones every prior add from the same actor with the same key in the causal past. See zh/models/flow-and-message.md §9.8 for the authoritative Reaction model (target scope, OR-Set, authz, anti-abuse) and zh/crypto-media/encryption-and-audit.md §2.9 for the plaintext-vs-encrypted policy.

key.description: Reaction key. Plaintext realms SHOULD use a single Unicode emoji cluster or registered short tag. End-to-end-encrypted realms with `aad_visibility != opaque_id` MUST carry the v1 keyed-HMAC routing tag here (`HMAC-SHA256(key = MLS-Exporter("cokret-reaction-routing-v1", context = realm_id), data = NFC(canonical_emoji))`), naturally bound to the current MLS group + epoch via the exporter secret; see zh/crypto-media/encryption-and-audit.md §2.9 for the authoritative construction. This lets OR-Set dedup, rate-limit and reducer convergence keep working without revealing the chosen emoji; the canonical emoji travels in `encrypted_payload`.

annotation.description: Optional free-form annotation (e.g. issue triage label). MUST be omitted when `encrypted_payload` is present; in E2EE realms the annotation MUST instead be carried inside `encrypted_payload`.

encrypted_payload.description: Encrypted carrier for the canonical reaction key and any annotation in E2EE realms. The decrypted plaintext JSON MUST validate as #/$defs/reaction_encrypted_payload_plaintext. When present, outer plaintext `key` MUST be the routing tag and `annotation` MUST be omitted; service-side OR-Set convergence still uses the outer routing key.

reaction_encrypted_payload_plaintext.description: Plaintext JSON encrypted into reaction_payload.encrypted_payload.ciphertext for ck.reaction.add / ck.reaction.remove in E2EE realms. The outer reaction_payload.key remains required and carries the service-visible routing tag; this plaintext carries the real reaction key and optional user content.

key.description: Canonical reaction key after client-side normalization: a single NFC Unicode emoji cluster or profile-registered short tag. This is the real reaction key, not the outer HMAC routing tag.

annotation.description: Optional user-visible annotation associated with the reaction.

remove_add_event_ids.description: Optional client-side convergence accelerator for ck.reaction.remove: add event ids that this remove intends to tombstone. MUST be omitted on ck.reaction.add. Service-side reducers still rely on the outer event actor_id, target_ref, key, and causal frontier.

progress_basis_points.description: Progress in basis points (0..10000 = 0%..100%). v1 wire forbids non-integer numbers; producers MUST use integer scaled forms.

cancelled_by.description: Set when status=cancelled: the actor that cancelled the session. See zh/extensions/agent-protocol-interop.md §5.3.

reason_code.description: Set when status=cancelled: machine-readable cancellation reason.

external_cancel_ref.description: Optional external-protocol cancellation reference for the cancelled session.

cleanup_required.description: Set when status=cancelled: cleanup steps the canceller / host MUST perform.

result_objects.description: Protocol objects materialized by the completed interop session.

agent_key_scope.description: Closed authorization scope for an agent signing key. Resource selectors and actions are both explicit so the key cannot silently widen its authority through omitted dimensions.

agent_key_approval_evidence.description: Evidence that authorized this agent key. High-risk keys MUST carry an approval/proposal/capability reference that can be replayed at the event frontier.

agent_key_authorize_payload.description: Payload for ck.agent.key.authorize. Binds one concrete agent signing key to an accountable principal, explicit agent_key_scope, audience, validity window, and approval evidence.

public_key_digest.description: Digest of the public key material behind verification_method. Required by high-assurance profiles when DID resolution is not pinned in the same seal batch.

revocation_check_ref.description: Optional freshness source for revocation checking. Absence does not waive expires_at.

runtime_attestation.description: Optional runtime / workload attestation captured at pairing approval time (CKP-0008 §4.5). v1 enum includes self_asserted as baseline; future profiles MAY register TEE / SLSA / SPIFFE attestation kinds. Implementations encountering an unknown kind MUST fail closed.

kind.description: v1 enum. Future profiles MAY extend via accepted attestation taxonomy.

attestation_digest.description: Optional digest of verifiable attestation material when kind is not self_asserted.

evidence_ref.description: Optional external verifiable attestation reference (TEE quote, SLSA provenance, etc.).

agent_key_revoke_payload.description: Payload for ck.agent.key.revoke. The or_set cell subject is (agent_principal_id, key_id); future protocol proofs from this key fail closed once this event is accepted.

revocation_frontier.description: Principal / Realm auth-state frontier under which this revocation was accepted.

agent_key_rotate_payload.description: Payload for ck.agent.key.rotate. key_id names the retiring key used as the cell subject; replacement_key_id names the new key. Reducers MUST verify the accountable_principal_id is unchanged, agent_key_scope is equivalent or narrower, and expires_at does not extend the retiring key's effective TTL.

agent_lifecycle_frontier.description: Auth/key/grant freshness frontier captured when accepting an agent lifecycle transition.

agent_sidecar_exposure_ack.description: Controller acknowledgement of sidecar Circles that became newly visible or eligible while the agent was paused.

agent_pause_payload.description: Payload for ck.agent.pause. The status cell is keyed by agent_principal_id and moves from active to paused under the captured freshness frontier.

agent_resume_payload.description: Payload for ck.agent.resume. Reducers re-check controller, agent, key, capability, Realm policy, accountability grant, and any sidecar exposure acknowledgement before returning the agent to active.

agent_deactivate_payload.description: Payload for ck.agent.deactivate. The terminal transition binds revocation fan-out to the same freshness frontier used to reject future agent sessions.

agent_action_target.description: Minimal target descriptor for an actor-private agent draft or approval. It identifies the eventual shared write surface without disclosing private draft content.

agent_draft_propose_payload.description: Payload for ck.agent.draft.propose. Actor-private proposal that may materialize into controller-owned encrypted draft account data after policy checks.

agent_action_request_payload.description: Payload for ck.agent.action_request. Actor-private request for controller approval before a shared Realm write is emitted.

agent_action_approve_payload.description: Payload for ck.agent.action_approve. Controller approval binds the draft/action request, target, approved payload digest, expiry, and single-use nonce.

agent_action_reject_payload.description: Payload for ck.agent.action_reject. Controller rejection terminates a draft/action request without shared Realm side effects.

consent_grant_payload.description: Holder-private consent grant. The actor (consenter) is the holder; payload.peer is the counterparty whose contact is consented to. Wire-equivalent to a Move whose effect is add(tag,value) on the cell ck:cell:ck.component.consent.grant.v1:<consent_id> (or_set lattice); ck.consent.revoke writes a remove on the same cell. Lives in the holder's Principal Control Realm (or holder-private actor stream); MUST NOT be written to a shared Collaboration Realm. Realm role taxonomy: zh/models/realm-and-space.md §2.7.

consent_id.description: Stable identifier; used as the cell_subject of the consent cell. ck.consent.revoke MUST reference the same consent_id.

peer.description: Counterparty DID (or pairwise DID) that this consent applies to.

consent_scope.description: What kind of contact is consented to. 'invite' = peer may send Realm / Flow invites; 'direct_message' = peer may initiate 1:1 message; 'voice_call' / 'video_call' = peer may initiate WebRTC call; 'presence' = peer may observe presence; 'any' = full consent across all consent scopes.

constraints.description: Optional consent-specific constraints (rate limits, time-of-day windows, device restrictions). v1 does not standardise constraint types beyond capability constraint vocabulary.

evidence_ref.description: Optional reference to claim disclosure, presentation response, or invite proof that triggered this consent (audit trail).

consent_revoke_payload.description: Revoke a previously granted consent. Wire-equivalent to a Control Move whose effect is remove(tag) on the consent cell ck:cell:ck.component.consent.grant.v1:<consent_id> (the same cell written by ck.consent.grant). Payload observed_dots MUST match the Control Move effect's observed_dots so schema validation and audit can see exactly what was removed.

consent_id.description: MUST equal the consent_id of the ck.consent.grant being revoked.

observed_dots.description: Exact add dots being removed. A full revoke, including consent_scope=any cascade, MUST enumerate every active dot that becomes inactive; implicit cascade without dot enumeration is invalid.

contact_requested_payload.description: Principal-scoped contact request fact. Issuer is the requester; target is the holder being asked to accept. This fact lives in the requester's Principal Control Realm and may be mirrored by the target as the original signed envelope.

request_id.description: SHOULD equal the enclosing ck.contact.requested event_id.

requester_consent_refs.description: Consent grant event refs written by requester for every requested scope.

contact_accepted_payload.description: Principal-scoped contact accept fact. Issuer is the original request target; requester is the peer whose request was accepted. Accepting writes target-controlled consent grants and references them here.

contact_rejected_payload.description: Principal-scoped contact rejection fact. Issuer is the original request target. Rejecting does not grant or revoke consent by itself.

contact_tombstoned_payload.description: Principal-scoped holder tombstone for one contact relation view. Issuer is the holder ending their side of the contact. Default revocation scope is contact-managed active consent dots only.

direct_conversation_bound_payload.description: Principal-scoped signed binding from an unordered participant pair to the canonical DM Realm and main Flow. Issuer MUST be one of the participants; the original signed envelope may be mirrored by the other participant.

pair_key.description: Canonical unordered pair key; must be based on stable subject/pairwise DID normalization and trust domain, never on handle strings.

member_event_refs.description: Membership event refs proving both participants are active members of the DM Realm.

invite_delivery_target.description: Public durable target for private invite delivery. payload.invitee is the subject; this object carries only the recipient Principal Server service DID.

introduction_evidence_digest.description: Digest of private invite delivery introduction_evidence. Raw locator tokens and receive-policy state MUST NOT appear in durable Realm events.

expires_at.description: Invite expiry timestamp. Directed v1 invite creates MUST carry it; reducers MUST NOT infer indefinite validity.

verification_method.description: DID URL with required key fragment. Method-name normalized to lowercase per W3C DID 1.0; matches the strict form used by $defs/verification_method elsewhere in this schema.

recovery_session_id.description: Present when this authorization was produced by a device recovery flow (crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §15). Binds the event to the recovery_session_id used by the proof transcript, backup-decrypt proofs, and the recovery_receipt, so an auditor reading only the control stream can correlate authorization to receipt. Omitted for ordinary pairing-based authorizations. Not part of the cross_signing_binding signing input (§5.2).

revocation_frontier.description: Principal control stream frontier under which this device revocation was accepted. Shared Realm MLS Remove commits that rely on the revocation must cover this frontier directly or through an imported governance Move.

key_backup_active_series_payload.description: Payload for ck.key_backup.active_series. The standalone ck.schema.key_backup_active_series.v1 schema carries the authoritative signed active-series record shape.

cross_signing_publish_payload.description: Payload for ck.cross_signing.publish. Schema ck.schema.cross_signing_publish.v1 (cross-signing-publish.schema.json) carries the authoritative shape; this payload entry mirrors the required-field set so the kind-specific payload class is wired into event-payload.schema.json dispatch. See device-lifecycle.md §5.1.

cross_signing_reset_payload.description: Payload for ck.cross_signing.reset. Schema ck.schema.cross_signing_reset.v1 (cross-signing-reset.schema.json) carries the authoritative shape; this payload entry mirrors the required-field set so the kind-specific payload class is wired into event-payload.schema.json dispatch. See device-lifecycle.md §14.1.

keypackage_digest.description: Canonical hash of the claimed MLS KeyPackage bytes. MUST equal the referenced ck.mls.keypackage.payload.keypackage_digest and claim_ref.keypackage_digest.

claim_ref.description: KeyPackage claim binding used by the receiver before decrypting the Welcome. claim_id, keypackage_ref, and keypackage_digest must match the top-level fields; capabilities_digest is sha256(JCS(claimed_capabilities)) from the single-use claim response; ssk_generation is the accepted cross-signing generation used when the claim was issued.

keypackage_digest.description: Canonical hash of the MLS KeyPackage bytes identified by keypackage_ref.

sender_device_signature.description: Detached device signature over canonical share metadata and ciphertext reference; verifiers MUST bind sender_device_id, recipient_principal_id, recipient_device_id, key_scope, aad_digest?, ciphertext/encrypted_key_ref and created_at.

effective_scope.description: Tagged scope of the key material. Realm-default history uses {kind:'realm', realm_id}; Circle history uses {kind:'circle', realm_id, circle_id}. Implementations MUST NOT infer key scope from flow_id or track.

policy_digest.description: Hash of the effective Realm/Circle policy root used to authorize this historical key share.

membership_frontier_digest.description: Optional hash of the membership frontier evaluated for history visibility and recipient membership.

realm_id.description: Parent Realm identifier. MUST equal effective_scope.realm_id.

circle_id.description: Present only when effective_scope.kind='circle'. MUST equal effective_scope.circle_id.

effective_scope.description: Tagged MLS governance scope. Realm-default groups use {kind:'realm', realm_id}; Circle groups use {kind:'circle', realm_id, circle_id}. This field, not Flow id or track, determines key and membership scope.

mls_governance_binding.$comment: Schema requires the tagged scope and circle_id presence rules. Reducers/verifiers must additionally compare realm_id == effective_scope.realm_id and, for circle scope, circle_id == effective_scope.circle_id; JSON Schema cannot express cross-field equality for these string values.

mls_genesis_payload.$comment: Schema requires both effective_scope and governance_binding. Reducers/verifiers must additionally compare effective_scope with governance_binding.effective_scope; JSON Schema cannot express deep cross-field equality.

effective_scope.description: Tagged scope of the MLS group created at epoch 0. MUST match governance_binding.effective_scope.

base_epoch.description: Expected previous MLS epoch. MUST equal governance_binding.previous_epoch.

next_epoch.description: Committed next MLS epoch. MUST equal governance_binding.next_epoch.

applet_registration_payload.description: Payload for ck.applet.registration. Durable Realm-history Event registering an Applet (bridge / bot / Ghost Actor namespace). Field vocabulary: zh/extensions/applet-integration.md §4 and zh/extensions/applet-schema.md §1 (the authoritative machine schema is applet.schema.json, which documents the applet object snapshot; the wire Event payload is this closed class). An Applet's capability to enter a Realm MUST be granted by that Realm's owner / admin / authorized registry-authz service; a self-signed registration alone MUST NOT write to a Realm (reason=applet_registration_unauthorized). registration MUST be signed by the controller DID (proof per models/event-and-patch.md §3).

applet_id.description: Stable applet identifier: a DID or the typed-id form ck:applet:<uuidv7>.

service_did.description: DID of the service hosting the applet runtime.

controller_did.description: DID of the Applet controller / external system; signs the registration.

namespaces.description: Applet namespace claims (actors / realms / handles patterns). Namespace match alone never grants write capability.

manifest.description: Applet manifest snapshot (capability requirements, supported intents, etc.).

proof.description: Controller-DID detached signature over the canonical registration object (excluding proof). An empty proof object MUST be rejected as schema_violation; required proof fields per models/event-and-patch.md §3.

applet_bridge_error_payload.description: Payload for ck.applet.bridge_error. Durable Realm-history Event recording a bridge / external-network failure. Field table: zh/extensions/applet-schema.md §7. MUST bind realm_id, failed_transaction_ref, retriable, and visibility_scope; missing any required field MUST be rejected as schema_violation. MUST NOT inline unauthorized external plaintext.

failed_transaction_ref.description: Reference to the failed transaction / source Event. MUST NOT inline unauthorized external plaintext.

error_class.description: Closed error category for aggregation / alerting. See zh/extensions/applet-schema.md §7.

visibility_scope.description: Visibility scope enum for the error event (e.g. realm_admins / applet_controller / realm_members). Clients MUST honor it and MUST NOT expose bridge-internal detail to unrelated members.

external_ref.description: External network reference (protocol / network id). MUST NOT contain unauthorized external plaintext.

message.description: Human-readable summary. MUST NOT leak unauthorized external plaintext.

retry_after_ms.description: Suggested retry delay; meaningful only when retriable=true.

applet_interop_session_start_payload.description: Payload for ck.applet.interop_session.start. Parallel to ck.agent.interop_session.start but applet-scoped. Field vocabulary: applet.schema.json (session_id correlates start/status; params are caller-supplied, opaque to soland and interpreted per applet manifest). Unlike ck.agent.* there is NO canonical applet session state machine in v1.

session_id.description: Per-invocation correlation id pairing start with the matching status event.

params.description: Caller-supplied parameters. Opaque to soland; bridge interprets per applet manifest.

applet_interop_session_status_payload.description: Payload for ck.applet.interop_session.status. Parallel to ck.agent.interop_session.status but applet-scoped. runtime_status is the bridge-implementation-defined status (applet.schema.json) — v1 does NOT mandate a canonical applet session state machine; the field is named runtime_status (not status) to keep applet snapshots distinguishable from the canonical agent session state machine. detail is a free-form bridge-side surface.

runtime_status.description: Bridge-implementation-defined runtime status. Bridges MAY restrict the set further in their applet manifest.

detail.description: Bridge-side detail surface (echo response, error context, bridge identifier, etc.). Bridges document their own schema.

mimi_room_binding_payload.description: Payload for ck.mimi.room_binding. Writes the ck.component.mimi.room_binding.v1 cell whose subject is payload.mimi_room_uri (see event-kind-registry.json cell_subject). Authoritative field set: zh/extensions/mimi-interop.md §3. The binding is a projection of a Cokret Realm/Flow discussion track into a MIMI room; it is not canonical truth. Creation / update / revocation MUST hold ck.policy.manage, ck.realm.admin, or an equivalent interop capability. E2EE MIMI rooms MUST bind mls_group_id and pass the MLS Governance Binding covered_seals_cell precondition.

mimi_room_uri.description: MIMI room URI. Cell subject for ck.component.mimi.room_binding.v1.

binding_scope.description: Cokret Realm + Flow scope this MIMI room projects. flow_id MUST point at an accepted Flow with discussion track enabled inside realm_id; the MIMI room timeline only projects that Flow's discussion track.

hub_provider.description: Service DID explicitly delegated by Realm policy, Organization DID, or participant DID to host the hub role.

mls_group_id.description: MLS group id. MUST be present for E2EE MIMI rooms.

status.description: Lifecycle state of the binding. accepted bindings authorize projection; revoked bindings stop new MIMI writes (only backfill / tombstone / report / legal hold / migration proof maintenance remains).

effective_scope.description: Governance boundary for the report. Defaults to the Realm scope when absent; Circle-scoped targets MUST resolve to the target Circle and route only to scoped moderators/admins.

moderation_decision_payload.description: Payload for ck.moderation.decision. An sealed moderation decision that writes an or_set add effect onto the ck.component.moderation_state.v1 cell whose subject is target_ref (the moderated target_event_id / target_object_id canonical string). See zh/authz/policy-server.md §7.1 and zh/governance/content-moderation.md §2.6 / §8.1. The decision verb is the runtime result set hard_deny / soft_deny / quarantine / require_review (all lower snake_case; allow is never sealed and soft_deny does not itself write the cell). The optional action carries the finer-grained §5.3 moderation_policy action family. The actor MUST independently hold ck.realm.moderation_policy or ck.policy.manage; refs[role=authorized_by] SHOULD reference the Policy Server signed decision for audit (not a capability source).

target_ref.description: The moderated target (event / object). Canonical string of this ref is the ck.component.moderation_state.v1 cell subject.

decision.description: Runtime decision verb (content-moderation.md §2.5 / §8.1). Lower snake_case; implementations MUST NOT introduce uppercase or camelCase variants.

action.description: Optional finer-grained §5.3 moderation_policy action family entry that the decision verb maps to (content-moderation.md §8.1).

reason_code.description: Machine-readable diagnostic. Values that cross service or federation boundaries MUST be registered in error-code-registry.json reason_codes.

policy_decision_ref.description: Reference to the Policy Server signed decision used as risk evidence. Audit / replay only; not a capability source.

modify_decision_ref.description: Set when this decision is the new decision emitted atomically by an appeal verdict=modify (content-moderation.md §5.5.2); reducer verifies it matches the same-batch appeal event id.

moderation_decision_lift_payload.description: Payload for ck.moderation.decision.lift. Writes an or_set remove effect on the same ck.component.moderation_state.v1 cell, removing the tag previously added by the decision identified by decision_ref. See zh/authz/policy-server.md §7.1 and zh/governance/content-moderation.md §5.5.2 (appeal verdict=overturn MUST pair a lift whose target equals decision_ref in the same ordered submit batch or equivalent control transaction).

target_ref.description: The moderated target whose ck.component.moderation_state.v1 cell the lift mutates. Same cell subject as the original ck.moderation.decision.

decision_ref.description: Reference to the prior ck.moderation.decision Event whose sealed tag is being removed.

audit_applet_binding_payload.description: Payload for ck.audit.applet_binding. Declares a non-retroactive audit applet/service binding for a Realm or Circle effective_scope. Binding is control-plane only and does not make the applet an MLS member or realtime sync recipient. Messages encrypted before activation_frontier_digest / first_auditable_epoch are never eligible for this binding's ck.audit.release.

activation_frontier_digest.description: Accepted Seal coverage digest at which this binding/policy became member-visible. Release requests MUST NOT cover messages or epochs before this coverage point.

first_auditable_epoch.description: First MLS epoch eligible for this binding. Reducers MUST verify it is the epoch created by a ck.mls.commit covering activation_frontier_digest; earlier epochs are permanently ineligible.

retroactive_release.description: v1 audited E2EE never permits a later binding or policy expansion to make pre-activation messages auditable.

eligibility_basis.description: A message is eligible only if it was encrypted after a commit covering this binding/policy frontier.

max_lookback_ms.description: Optional maximum age, measured from session request/authorization time, for otherwise eligible material. Later policy changes may narrow this for future messages but MUST NOT expand already encrypted messages.

max_epoch_span.description: Optional cap on the number of sealed historical epochs a single session/release may cover.

allowed_target_classes.description: Optional target class allow-list for targeted_evidence_release.

audit_session_payload.description: Shared payload class for ck.audit.session.request / authorize / notice / close. The stage field identifies which lifecycle step this event represents; reducers validate the step-specific state machine against the enclosing Event.kind.

audit_release_payload.description: Payload for ck.audit.release. A sealed audit release manifest for a bounded historical window. It records release metadata and wrapped material digests only; plaintext MUST NOT be inlined.

eligibility_proof.description: Proof summary that the requested release is inside the binding activation frontier, first_auditable_epoch, release_window_policy, and the targets' encryption-time eligibility snapshots.

activation_commit_ref.description: ck.mls.commit that covered the activation frontier and created first_auditable_epoch, when the release covers MLS epoch material.

policy_snapshot_digest.description: Digest of the binding/release window policy snapshot used when authorizing this release.

target_eligibility_digest.description: Digest of the deterministic per-target/per-epoch eligibility set proving no pre-activation material is included.

audit_accessed_payload.description: Strict payload for ck.audit.accessed. It records a specific access or paired privacy-sensitive write. Reducers MUST reject business events that require an audit pair unless this payload identifies the same writer, target, and object/cell in the same ordered submit batch, equivalent control transaction, or an accepted pre-read event with RYW receipt.

late_recovery_original_event_id.description: Required when access_kind=e2ee_late_recovery; identifies the original encrypted event whose plaintext became available through late key recovery.

ryw_required.description: When true, plaintext release or privileged projection MUST wait for an accepted-history RYW receipt before disclosure.

participant_binding.description: Token issuer's signed commitment over (realm_id, call_id, focus_id, actor_id, device_id, participant_identity, expires_at) for a media participant. See crypto-media/media-service-binding.md §3 and crypto-media/call-state.md §4.1. v1 uses the single scheme ck.media.participant_binding.v1.

issuer_kid.description: DID URL (with fragment) of the token issuer service signing key. MUST resolve to a service DID present in the current-epoch ck.realm.media_service.service_id.

call_participant.description: A single participant entry in ck.call.state.payload.participants[]. See crypto-media/call-state.md §4/§4.1.

foci_preferred.description: Client-local ordered focus preference list used for the session_focus election (see crypto-media/call-state.md §4.1 and media-service-binding.md §5).

call_state_payload.description: Typed payload for ck.call.state (durable call lifecycle state). state is a controlled enum, participants carry machine-checkable participant_binding, and recording results are carried in a typed recording_result object. See crypto-media/call-state.md §4/§4.1/§5.

session_focus.description: Single authoritative focus_id for this call. reducer write rule per crypto-media/call-state.md §4.1: committed once, any rewrite MUST failed_precondition reason=session_focus_already_committed.

recording_state.description: Recording lifecycle, orthogonal to `state` (the recording dimension of a call, independent of call lifecycle). Absent = no recording. 'recording' = capture in progress (after ck.call.recording.start); 'stopped' = recording manually stopped without requiring an artifact; 'ready' = artifact available via the Cokret blob pipeline; 'failed' = recording failed. recording_result SHOULD accompany recording_state ∈ {stopped, ready, failed}. See crypto-media/call-state.md §5.

recording_result.description: Typed recording outcome, present when recording_state ∈ {stopped, ready, failed}. See crypto-media/call-state.md §4.2 / §5: the durable ck.call.state carries recording_start_event_id for every terminal recording segment, and carries content digest, duration, media type and retention policy when an artifact exists. All fields optional at schema level; prose defines state-specific requirements.

board_space_id.description: Board Space that owns the position edge; deduplication key (board_space_id, flow_id) MUST be unique among active edges.

from_space_id.description: Source List Space (optional; reducer infers from current active edge if omitted).

target_space_id.description: Target List Space after move. This is the ONLY payload-level field for the destination; the reducer compiles it into the cas_register cell value as 'list_space_id' on the cell at ck:cell:ck.component.flow.position.v1:<board_space_id>:<flow_id>. Writers MUST NOT put 'list_space_id' directly on the ck.flow.move payload (additionalProperties=false enforces this) — there is exactly one destination input field on the wire.

space_id.description: List Space within which the reorder happens.

flow_watch_set_payload.description: Payload for ck.flow.watch.set. Writes the (flow_id, watcher_actor_id) watch cell. The new cell value is computed from payload.level + payload.level_public: when level is null the effect is set null (clear, equivalent to mentions_only); when level is a string the effect is set { level, level_public? }. Reducer invariants: (1) watcher_actor_id MUST equal envelope.actor_id unless writer holds ck.flow.watch.set.others; (2) when watcher_actor_id != envelope.actor_id (.others write), level MUST be one of {mentions_only, participating, all} and level_public MUST be omitted or false — writing muted or level_public=true on behalf of another actor MUST failed_precondition; (3) .others writes MUST carry refs[role=audit_pair] to a same-batch ck.audit.accessed event whose payload access_kind=watch_set_others identifies writer / target / cell / before-after heads. See models/flow-and-message.md §8.4.

level.description: Watch level. Required. null clears the cell (equivalent to mentions_only / no record); in that case level_public MUST be omitted.

level_public.description: Opt-in publication of the level value to non-self projection consumers. Default false. muted MUST NOT be exposed even with level_public=true. MUST be omitted when level is null.

expected_value.description: Compiles to cas_register head_eq precondition. Whole-value compare against the cell pre-state: either null (assert no prior record) or { level, level_public? } matching the prior cell value exactly. When omitted, reducers MUST treat it as head_eq null: only the initial write may pass; an existing cell MUST fail_precondition. Omission MUST NOT disable CAS or imply last-write-wins.

allOf.description: level_public MUST be omitted when level is null (clearing a cell does not carry a public-level setting).
